anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceiver U11 has its logic-side supply pin VCC1 (pin 1) connected to the 5V_switched_CAN rail, while the MCP2515 CAN controller U8 is powered from SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V (pin 18).
anomalies.expected: The logic-side supply of the isolated CAN transceiver should match the I/O voltage of the MCP2515 controller (3.3V) to avoid overvoltage on the RXD/TXD logic lines.

evidence.quote: U11 pin 1 VCC1 connected to net 5V_switched_CAN; U8 pin 18 VDD connected to net SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V (CAN BUS sheet).
U8, U9 — MCP2515-xSO CAN controllers; ... U11 (and its CAN1 counterpart) — isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The 5V logic output from U11 RXD may exceed the MCP2515 input voltage rating when U8 is powered at 3.3V, potentially damaging the CAN controller or causing unreliable communication.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a likely power-domain mismatch on the isolated CAN transceiver U11: its logic-side VCC1 is tied to 5V_switched_CAN while the MCP2515 controller U8 runs from 3.3V, which can overstress the CAN controller logic pins.
